We need a prime \(p\) such that there is an integer \(n\) with  

\[
n^{4}+1\equiv 0 \pmod{p^{2}} .
\]

Let \(f(x)=x^{4}+1\).  
If \(x_0\) satisfies \(f(x_0)\equiv 0 \pmod{p}\) and \(f'(x_0)\not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}\), then by Hensel’s lemma the solution lifts uniquely to a solution modulo \(p^{2}\).

Thus \(p\) must satisfy

\[
-1\text{ is a fourth power modulo }p
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x^{4}\equiv -1 \pmod{p}
\]

for some \(x\).  
In the cyclic group \((\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^{\times}\) of order \(p-1\) this happens exactly when the group contains an element of order \(8\).  
An element of order \(8\) exists iff \(8\mid p-1\).

Hence the smallest prime with \(p-1\equiv 0\pmod{8}\) is

\[
p=17 .
\]

Indeed, for \(p=17\) we have \(8\mid 16\), and a solution exists: \(n=2\) gives \(2^{4}+1=17\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**Step 2 –  Find the minimal \(m\) with \(m^{4}+1\equiv 0\pmod{289}\).**

We must solve

\[
m^{4}\equiv -1 \pmod{289}\qquad (289=17^{2}).
\]

First find the solutions modulo \(17\).  
Computing \(x^{4}\bmod 17\) gives

\[
x\equiv 2,\,8,\,9,\,15 \pmod{17}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^{4}\equiv 16\equiv-1\pmod{17}.
\]

For each root \(x\) we lift it to a root modulo \(289\) using the binomial expansion

\[
(x+17k)^{4}\equiv x^{4}+4x^{3}\cdot 17k\pmod{289},
\]

because all higher–order terms are multiples of \(17^{2}\).

Let \(x^{4}=17t-1\) (so \(t=(x^{4}+1)/17\)).  
Then

\[
x^{4}+4x^{3}\cdot 17k \equiv-1
\;\Longrightarrow\;
t+4x^{3}k\equiv 0\pmod{17}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
k\equiv -t\,(4x^{3})^{-1}\pmod{17}.
\]

---
